observation.visible_scene: A calm alpine lake framed by a rocky, boulder-strewn shoreline in the foreground with a pale fallen log lying across it, a small green grass tuft, and a cluster of dark conifers at the left edge. Across the water a thin band of evergreens lines the far shore, behind which a snow-capped peak sits centered under a blue sky with wispy clouds and a brighter cloud mass at the upper right. The still water mirrors the peak and tree line.
visible_changes: Over the first few frames (t=0.0 to ~0.2 s) the image transitions from a hazy, low-saturation look (grayish-green rocks, washed-out sky) to a more saturated, higher-contrast rendering (brownish rocks, deeper blue sky); after this settling the overall color/exposure stays roughly constant through the last frame.
The mountain reflection in the lake remains present and stable throughout, with no visible ripple disturbance.
Foreground rocks, the fallen log, the grass tuft, and the conifers keep the same positions relative to the frame edges across the excerpt.
Cloud shapes in the sky show at most very slight, gradual change; no discrete movement or morph is clearly resolvable between sampled frames.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the opening color shift is a fade-in from a prior shot or an in-camera exposure/grading adjustment is not determinable from these frames.
Any cloud motion or camera drift before t=0 or after t=2.67 s is outside the segment.
Whether the water is genuinely wind-still or only appears so at this sampling rate is not established.
uncertain_details: Camera is effectively static; any sub-pixel pan/zoom or drift cannot be confirmed from the background evidence.
Cloud drift, if present, is too small to verify as continuous motion versus sampling noise.
The exact timing and smoothness of the saturation/contrast settling is approximate given the discrete frames.
